Seattle, Washington · coffee

Coffee in Seattle for cyclists

Where riders in Seattle start the day and finish the ride. Open early, near the routes, fine with a table of people in bibs. The ones marked ride-out sit at a group ride’s start; the note says which ride and when.

For: Seattle to Portland Bicycle Classic.

Coffee in Seattle for cyclists, listed

  1. Tailwind Cafe & Bar

    1424 11th Ave, Seattle, WA 98122 · 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. Tuesday to Sunday, closed Monday

    ride-out

    Capitol Hill, in the alley at Chophouse Row, with a courtyard. Good Weather’s Sunday Social (Sundays, 10:30 am) meets here and rolls half an hour later; the café opens at 9, so there is time for coffee first. Espresso, breakfast and sandwiches, beer and wine; indoor and outdoor seating, tip-free, per its site. Closed Monday. Nothing on its page says bike parking.

    The ride from here: Good Weather Sunday Social (Sundays, 10:30 am) →

  2. PIM Bicycles & Coffeehouse

    4013 Leary Way NW, Seattle, WA 98107 · 6 a.m. to 2 p.m. Monday and Friday, 7 to 2 Saturday and Sunday; Tuesday to Thursday not listed

    A bike shop with a coffee bar “located right on the Burke-Gilman trail” in Fremont, in its own words. Opens at 6 on Monday and Friday and 7 on the weekend, the earliest door this guide found near the trail. Walk-ins for quick fixes, per the shop page. Tuesday to Thursday hours weren’t listed; call 206-784-2097 first midweek. Nothing on its pages says a pump or bike parking; it has a car lot.

  3. Pacha Collective

    7119 Woodlawn Ave NE, Seattle, WA 98115 · 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Monday to Friday, 7 to 5 Saturday and Sunday

    Green Lake, on the same street as Gregg’s. An all-day café with coffee, bowls and a bar, open to 9 on weeknights. Brevay Cycling’s Thursday-morning WTFNB ride met here through September 2026; its series page showed no upcoming date on Oct 4, 2026, so check the ride’s own listing before you plan a morning around it. Nothing on the café’s page says bike parking.

  4. Cafe Allegro

    4214 University Way NE, Seattle, WA 98105 · 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. weekdays, 8 to 6 weekends

    The U District, a block from the STP hotels, with the entrance in the alley. Espresso roasted on site. Opens at 7 on weekdays and 8 on weekends, so it is the coffee the day before the STP and the morning after, not the 5 a.m. start. Nothing on its page says outdoor seating or bike parking.

  5. Pegasus Coffee House

    131 Parfitt Way SW, Bainbridge Island, WA 98110 · 7 a.m. daily; closes 4 to 6 p.m. depending on the day

    The coffee on the ferry-and-island day: Winslow, off the Seattle ferry, on the Chilly Hilly course. Opens at 7 every day; its two pages give the close as 4, 5 or 6 depending on the day, so plan on 4. The same roaster has a weekday coffee bar downtown at 711 3rd Avenue, 6:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. Monday to Friday, on the side of town the ferry leaves from. Bike parking isn’t on either page. 206-317-6914.
